page: Microsoft Azure M64m is a memory-intensive server instance powered by the Intel Xeon 8280M processor. Running on the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor, it features 64 dedicated vCPUs mapped to 32 physical cores with hyper-threading enabled. The processor operates at a base clock speed of 2.7 GHz and includes 38 MB of L3 cache. The instance is equipped with 1792.0 GB of system memory, yielding a high memory-to-core ratio of 28.0 GB per core. Local storage is bundled with a capacity of 7340 GB, while there are no integrated GPUs.

Benchmark data indicates a clear contrast between single-core and multi-threaded performance. Single-core metrics, such as stress-ng single-core CPU performance and Geekbench single-core scores, fall into the bottom 10% tier. However, multi-threaded capabilities are more robust, with stress-ng multi-core CPU performance, Geekbench multi-core, and Passmark CPU scores aligning with average tier results. Notably, the instance demonstrates strong memory bandwidth for large uncached blocks, registering 182.37 GB/sec, and strong multi-threaded bzip3 decompression at 188.37 GB/sec. Conversely, single-threaded compression and decompression tasks remain weak.

Given its massive memory footprint and bundled 7340 GB local storage, the M64m is designed for memory-heavy workloads. It is highly suitable for large-scale relational databases, in-memory caching systems like Redis, and enterprise resource planning applications. While its single-core compute performance is relatively low, the high resource density of RAM and storage provides qualitative cost efficiency for workloads that prioritize memory capacity and multi-threaded throughput over raw single-threaded CPU speed.

It is highly suited for large-scale databases, in-memory data stores, and enterprise applications requiring substantial memory capacity and local storage without GPU acceleration.
